q: In project management, what does ITTO stand for?
options: Inputs, tools and techniques, and outputs
explanation: Each process is described by its inputs, tools and techniques, and outputs. The 8th edition lists sample ITTOs for each of its 40 processes.

q: Which document formally authorizes the existence of a project and gives the project manager authority to apply organizational resources?
explanation: The project charter is issued by the project initiator or sponsor, formally authorizes the project and provides the project manager with authority to use organizational resources.

q: To get started quickly, a project manager drafts the project charter and signs it herself. Who should issue the project charter?
explanation: The charter is issued by the project initiator or sponsor. The project manager may help develop it, but does not authorize their own project.

q: A company approves a charter, begins planning, and names a project manager only when executing starts. When should the project manager be identified and assigned?
options: After the project management plan is approved
Only once the first deliverable is due
As early as possible, ideally during charter development and always before planning begins
explanation: The project manager should be assigned as early as possible, ideally during development of the charter and always before planning begins.

options: A list of all project risks
A documented economic feasibility study used to establish the validity of the benefits of the project
explanation: The business case is a documented economic feasibility study. It gives the reasons and objectives for the project and is used at the end to measure success.

q: Why are the business case and the benefits management plan called business documents instead of project documents?
options: They are written by the project team during executing
They are developed before the project is initiated and are referenced again after it is completed
explanation: Both are developed prior to the project and referenced after it, so they are business documents, not project documents or components of the project management plan.

q: What does the project management plan describe?
options: How the project will be executed, monitored and controlled, and closed
Why the organization should invest its money and people in the project
The daily tasks of each team member
The list of issues found so far
explanation: The project management plan describes how the project will be executed, monitored and controlled, and closed. It is the basis for all project decisions and a living document.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Project management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Project management plan

q: An auditor asks which of the team's files are components of the project management plan and which are project documents. Which of the following is a project document and NOT a component of the project management plan?
explanation: The risk register is a project document. The risk management plan, scope management plan and schedule baseline are parts of the project management plan.

q: One task slipped, so a team member edits the approved schedule baseline directly to match. How can a baseline be changed?
options: By any team member, whenever the work requires it
Only through formal change control procedures
By the customer sending an email
explanation: A baseline is the approved version of a work product. It can be changed only using formal change control procedures and is the basis for comparison with actual results.

q: A team member records: 'Activity 7 started on 3 May, 120 hours spent so far.' This is an example of:
explanation: Raw observations and measurements taken while the work is performed are work performance data. They have not yet been compared with the plan.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance data

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance data

q: After comparing actual costs with the budget, the project manager concludes that the project is 8% over budget. This conclusion is:
explanation: Work performance information is data analyzed in comparison with the plan, which gives it context and shows how the project is performing.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance information

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance information

options: Work performance reports, then information, then data
Work performance information, then data, then reports
Work performance data, then reports, then information
Work performance data, then information, then reports
explanation: Raw data is collected during executing, analyzed into information by the controlling processes, and compiled into reports for stakeholders.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance reports

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Work performance reports

q: In a corridor conversation a stakeholder mentions that a report should have an extra column. The project manager explains that this is not yet a change request. What is a change request?
options: An informal suggestion mentioned in passing during a team meeting
A formal proposal to modify a document, deliverable or baseline
The final report at project closure
explanation: A change request is a formal proposal to modify a document, deliverable or baseline, and may be initiated inside or outside the project.

q: The project is two weeks behind schedule, so the project manager requests approval to add a second shift to catch up. Which type of change request is this?
explanation: A corrective action realigns current performance with the plan. A preventive action protects future performance; a defect repair fixes a nonconforming deliverable.

q: Which statement about verified and accepted deliverables is correct?
options: The team verifies a deliverable for correctness first; the customer or authorized stakeholder then accepts it
The customer verifies first; the team then accepts
A deliverable is accepted before it is built
explanation: Verified deliverables have been checked for correctness and become the input to formal acceptance. Accepted deliverables have been validated against criteria and approved.

q: Nine people vote on three options. The results are 4, 3 and 2 votes. The option with 4 votes is chosen. Which decision-making method was used?
explanation: With plurality the largest block decides even without a majority. A majority would need more than 50%, which is at least 5 of 9.

q: A project is still on budget and on schedule, but something in this month's review worries the project manager about the months ahead. Which of the following is a leading indicator?
options: The number of deliverables completed last month
Key stakeholders are not available or engaged
The cost variance at the end of the phase
explanation: Leading indicators give early warning of future problems, such as disengaged stakeholders or unclear success criteria. The other options measure the past and are lagging indicators.

q: What does the acronym SMART stand for?
explanation: SMART criteria help set clear, attainable and meaningful goals: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound.

q: Which governance model is typically used on more predictive projects?
options: Structured governance, with a sponsor, PMO leader, governance board and project manager
explanation: Structured governance is often used on more predictive projects. Self-governance, where the team ensures value is delivered, is more common on adaptive projects.
